message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to sell houses or declare bankruptcy to cover a $750 rent shortfall.

I have $616 cash but need $750. All properties are already mortgaged, so I must sell houses to cover the $134 shortfall. I can sell up to four houses from ORIENTAL_AVENUE, VERMONT_AVENUE, or CONNECTICUT_AVENUE.

Each house sells for $25. I need to sell six houses to cover the $134 shortfall. All three properties currently have four houses each, so I must keep them evenly distributed.

Selling two houses from each light blue property will raise $150. That covers the $134 shortfall and leaves $16 in cash. Five houses would not cover the debt.

Two houses on each light blue property yield only $90-$100 in rent. The opponent can easily afford that. Four houses would force bankruptcy, but I cannot keep them. Selling all twelve houses would raise $300 and leave $166 cash after paying the debt.

Selling three houses from each light blue would raise $225 but leave only $91 cash after paying the debt. One-house rents are too weak to threaten the opponent.

I am now assessing whether I can hurt p2 enough to win. p2 currently holds an orange monopoly with four houses on St James, Tennessee, and New York. They also have a dark blue set with three houses on Park Place and Boardwalk. Their red properties appear unmortgaged.

I am on p2's TENNESSEE_AVENUE, which explains the $750 rent. After the minimum sale, I will have only $16 left. Any further rent to p2 would bankrupt me. I am weighing whether to sell all houses now for a larger cash buffer or keep two houses as a defensive weapon.

Selling all houses now would not increase total liquidity. The same $166 could be raised later by selling the remaining houses at $25 each. Keeping houses provides a free upside: if p2 lands on them and pays rent, I gain cash without selling anything.

I realized keeping houses would tie up the bank's only two remaining houses. p2 cannot build more on their monopolies without those houses, so selling them back would give p2 the capital to expand their holdings.

p2 can already buy the two houses needed to complete their dark blue set. I have no other monopolies to expand, so selling my houses would only give p2 more capital to build on their existing holdings.

p2 can upgrade their orange monopoly to hotels without needing bank houses, since four houses return to the bank when a hotel is placed. They also own the red monopoly through Kentucky and Illinois, though Indiana is mortgaged and would need to be unmortgaged first. Ventnor belongs to me, so p2 cannot build there.

I am on TENNESSEE_AVENUE and p2 is on STATES_AVENUE. I paid rent because I landed there. p2 will roll from States next. That position is 13, so they are past my light blue properties and must go around the board.

The opponent cannot land on my houses this turn. From States, a single roll would require 33 spaces to reach Oriental, which is impossible. The rent upside is not immediate. Denying bank houses remains strategically useful if they attempt to build later.

I will sell two houses from each light blue property. I will keep the remaining six houses off the market to deny p2 building capital. The bank has only two houses left, so returning six would let them expand significantly. I will not reveal this strategy in my public message.
